newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Board battle brews over Utd Utilities.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Board battle brews over Utd Utilities.

text.p: Shares in Britain's United Utilities Plc held firm on Monday despite clear signs of a brewing boardroom tussle over the role of company management ahead of a crucial board meeting.

United Utilities shares rose 7-1/2 pence to 708-1/2. But despite being among the highest gainers in the utility sector on Monday, some analysts expect its share price to remain sluggish until a possible boardroom tangle is sorted out.
The tussle surrounds speculation over the role of United Utilities' chairman Desmond Pitcher who also has executive responsibilities, and the company's directors meet on Tuesday.
Some institutional shareholders, led by non executive director Peter Middleton, are expected to either press for Pitcher to take over a non-executive role or step down from the company's board.
A company spokesman told Reuters that the main item on the agenda of Tuesday's meeting will be a discussion on the views canvassed by Middleton.
Middleton, who is also chairman of Barclays Plc's investment banking unit BZW, has been canvassing opinion within the City on Pitcher's role.

"The meeting will discuss the views canvassed by Peter Middleton...it is the main item," the spokesman said. "It's a meeting with institutional investors on the future of the company's management," he said.
Middleton was not immediately available for comment.
Speculation on Pitcher's role surfaced after his surprise sacking of chief executive Brian Staples, while Staples was on holiday last month.

Staples became the second chief executive to be sacked in similar circumstances in the last four years, casting doubts on the need to have two executive roles at the head of the company's management structure.
United Utilities was formed in 1995 when North West Water bought its local regional electricity company Norweb.
The company's share price has fallen from levels of 770 pence after Staples was sacked and the utility division's managing director Derek Green was asked to take over.
Some analysts believe the uncertainty over the management's future could put the brakes on the share price despite it being considered as undervalued.

"I think the share price will not significantly outperform the market until they resolve the issue and they come out with something," an analyst said. "The share price will probably be dogged until the issue is sorted out," he said.
Based on fundamentals and performance ability, most analysts have pegged a share price target in the range of 750-760 pence.

"At the end of the day there's a good underlying business there with massive revenue flows from water and electricity and we are not talking about a key personality," said Yamaichi analyst, Nigel Hawkins.
